title: Teach strategies briefly, then build knowledge
statement: Teach comprehension strategies briefly and explicitly, inside the content they serve, and spend the rest of the time building knowledge through coherent sets of related texts.
example: Across eight quantitative reviews, about 10 strategy sessions gave the same comprehension benefit as about 50.
detail: The reading course's synthesis of five primary sources, every quote in it checked by script against the full texts, reports that across eight quantitative reviews more practice with a comprehension strategy gave no added benefit, ten sessions yielding the same as fifty, and that its authors concluded strategy instruction should be explicit and brief (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/SYNTHESIS.qmd`, lines 1-7 and 45-48). A research report it draws on adds that unless strategies are closely linked with knowledge in a content area, students are unlikely to learn them fully (the same file, lines 55-58).
against: The same synthesis holds that strategies genuinely work and that the claim is bounded value, not no value (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/reading-science/SYNTHESIS.qmd`, lines 172-176). The same synthesis warns that too wide a range of content and texts leaves strategies not fully learned, and too narrow a range makes transfer fail. The study was small and exploratory (N=59), its comprehension-questions measure was null, and knowledge transfer was near-domain at best (η²=.09) (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/SKILL.md`, `grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/applied/teaching-comprehension-insights-brainlift.qmd`). Explicit strategy instruction produces immediate use, but there is less evidence that students keep using the strategies after instruction ends (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`). Strategies do work: the reading-science synthesis calls the claim bounded value, not no value (`ti-courseplans-audit/docs/reading-science/SYNTHESIS.qmd`).

**Strategies genuinely work**
The claim is *bounded value*, not *no value*.
**One lesson is below the dose that worked.**
main-idea questioning does not transfer; the successful studies taught "explicitly, took place daily for considerable amounts of time, and continued across several weeks."
**It is an intervention guide, not core instruction.**
Recommendation 3 carries **"a strong level of evidence"**, from 34 studies, 23 meeting WWC standards without reservations.
If comprehension strategies are taught with an array of content and a range of texts that are too wide, then students will not fully learn them.
**conceptual coherence** ("repetition, elaboration, and examples provided across the texts," not merely sharing a topic) produced a large knowledge gain
- Direct, explicit comprehension-strategy instruction: strong.

the 4-step INFER frame is walked exactly once (p17 skill-steps, p18 infer-steps, both 'walk:true') then immediately used on story content across I-do/we-do/you-do, never re-drilled as an abstract skill.
